limits: Root full source read, before viewing extraction records/answers; not statistical blind certification. First results retained; used cases become development regressions.

cases.question: Did Tyler finally receive the boxed Ultima he was saving for?
cases.expected: Still seeking Ultima I baggie edition, not boxed; unpack/display routine is hypothetical, and he continues saving/searching.

cases.question: Was $538 what Tyler paid for his Geniac electric brain?
cases.expected: No. That is the stale listing he rejected, formerly $500. He bought a different one after more appeared, for an unspecified much lower amount.

cases.question: Which anniversary collection did Johnny actually say arrived, after correcting himself?
cases.expected: He first says Castlevania then explicitly corrects to Contra; it arrived and was scanned then shelved.
forbidden: Confirmed Castlevania arrival from this corrected claim

cases.question: Was Game Historia already operating as the hosts' museum?
cases.expected: No. Tyler describes a stalled website aimed at encouraging older-game play; the museum exchange is explicitly denied, and he does not call the site his definitive ultimate end goal.

cases.question: Why did Johnny warm to Phase Shift after initially objecting about singing?
cases.expected: Clarification: it supports singing but does not judge vocals. Initial no-vocal-support phrasing is qualified, and Johnny likes freedom from scoring.

cases.question: Did the hosts dismiss every part of the Wata guide as useless?
cases.expected: No. They find it useful process documentation for grading customers but less useful for ordinary collecting than the CGC guide; this is their episode-time judgment.
